headline: Laplace Intelligence red-teams physical AI before it hits the real world
summary: This startup uses AI to stress-test robots and self-driving cars in high-fidelity simulations, aiming to prevent real-world failures.
details: Laplace Intelligence is developing automated red-teaming for robotics and physical AI. Their goal is to discover and fix problems in AI systems before they are deployed in the physical world, ensuring safety and reliability.

The company leverages high-fidelity simulations reconstructed from real-world data, using platforms like Nvidia's Cosmos. These simulations can recreate diverse environments, from highways to city streets, with accurate scale and details.
Developers can interact with these simulations by using language prompts to alter environmental conditions, such as adding real-time traffic based on data from navigation providers like TomTom.

Laplace's unique selling proposition lies in its AI agents that automatically design corner cases and challenging scenarios. These agents can draw information from news and police reports to actively probe for weaknesses in AI systems.

The startup's approach is inspired by 'Laplace's demon,' a thought experiment about predicting the future with perfect knowledge. Laplace uses simulation to predict and mitigate potential failures in the physical world.
Founded by University of Michigan researchers Howie Sun and Henry Liu, Laplace is one of the startups competing in TechCrunch Disrupt's Startup Battlefield on October 13th.

headline_marked: Apple HomeView: [[Smart display launches]] for $299, but lacks EU support
headline: Apple HomeView: Smart display launches for $299, but lacks EU support
summary: Apple's new smart display is priced at $299, offering a glimpse into the company's HomeKit strategy. However, it won't be available in the European Union at launch.
details: Apple has officially launched its new smart display, dubbed HomeView, at a surprising price point of $299. This device aims to integrate more deeply into the Apple ecosystem, offering a central hub for smart home control and information.

The HomeView features a sleek design with a prominent display showing the time, weather, and calendar events. Early hands-on impressions highlight its potential as a seamless addition to existing Apple device setups.

While the $299 price is considered competitive for an Apple product of this nature, some users have noted that essential accessories, such as a wall mount, are sold separately and can cost an additional $59 minimum.

Interestingly, Apple has confirmed that HomeView will not be launching in the European Union at its initial release. The specific reasons for this exclusion have not been fully detailed by the company.
Questions remain about third-party app support on the HomeView. Apple has indicated that it is open to the possibility, but no concrete plans or timelines have been announced yet.
